primary.name: Reactive Balance Flow
primary.mantra: Quality over speed

steps.text: Single-leg stance, eyes open. Left leg.
steps.cue: Soft knee. Find a fixed point at eye level.

steps.text: Single-leg stance, eyes open. Right leg.
steps.cue: Tripod foot. Big toe, little toe, heel — all three pressing down.
Opposite hand to opposite knee. Reach with intention, not speed.
Small, controlled disturbances. Recover before the next.
Each wobble teaches the system. Stay with each one.
Whole body moves as one. Lead with the eyes.
Catch the moment. Reset. Catch again.
Notice what the system is doing without your direction.

primary.name: Animal Locomotion Practice
primary.mantra: Move like the body remembers

steps.text: Bear crawl, slow and quiet, 30 meters.
steps.cue: Knees hover, never touch. Hands and opposite feet move together.
Look between your hands. Trust the floor.
Hips up. The chest leads where you go.
Belly low. Elbow drives forward, opposite knee follows.
Hands plant first. Then both feet swing through.
Same pattern, opposite side.
Knee toward elbow on each step. Keep the hips low.

steps.text: Stand. Slow walk to recover, 60 seconds.
steps.cue: Notice how the body feels different now.

primary.name: Reaction & Timing Block
primary.mantra: Move on the cue, not before

steps.text: Stand ready, soft knees. Three slow breaths.
steps.cue: Calm body, ready mind.

steps.text: Self-cued lateral steps. Left, right, left, right.
steps.cue: Each step decisive. Plant fully before the next.

steps.text: Random direction stepping. Forward, back, side, diagonal.
steps.cue: Vary the direction. Don't repeat the same pattern.

steps.text: Ball drop reaction (use any small object).
steps.cue: Drop, then react. The pause before reaction is the practice.

steps.text: Mirror response. Move suddenly, reset, move again.
steps.cue: Sudden but controlled. Speed without sloppiness.

steps.text: Tempo-change drill. Slow, then fast, then slow again.
steps.cue: Same movement, different speed. Stay precise.
Let the nervous system absorb the work.

primary.name: Hand-Eye Coordination Block
primary.mantra: The eye leads, the hand follows

steps.text: Soft gaze, look far. Then close, then far. Three rounds.
steps.cue: Train the focus muscle before the hands move.

steps.text: Wall ball catches, dominant hand. Use any small ball.
steps.cue: Watch the ball into your hand. Don't anticipate.
The weaker hand needs more attention, not more force.
Catch, throw, catch, throw. Smooth handoffs.

steps.text: Cross-hand target touches. Touch your right knee with left hand, left knee with right.
steps.cue: Speed up only when the pattern is clean.

steps.text: Tracing shapes in the air, both hands together.
steps.cue: Symmetrical patterns. Mirror left and right.

steps.text: Stillness. Soft eyes. Notice the breathing.
steps.cue: Settle before you finish.

primary.name: Vestibular Awakening
primary.mantra: The system gets sharper through use

steps.text: Stand, head turns left and right, eyes following.
steps.cue: Slow at first. Let the inner ear track.

steps.text: Walking, head turning side to side.
steps.cue: Walk a straight line. Turn the head, not the path.

steps.text: Walking with gaze shifts. Look near, then far, then near.
steps.cue: Each shift is a recalibration.

steps.text: Gentle spin. Turn 360 degrees slowly. Recover.
steps.cue: Stop, plant, find a fixed point. The recovery is the practice.
Vary how you get up each time. Change the pattern.

steps.text: Direction-change walking. Walk, turn, stop, walk again.
steps.cue: Each turn is full presence.
The system is working harder than it looks. Trust it.

primary.name: Footwork Skill Block
primary.mantra: Light feet, full attention

steps.text: Quick feet in place, 30 seconds. Stop.
steps.cue: Stay on the balls of the feet. Light contact.

steps.text: Lateral shuffle, 20 meters each way, 3 rounds.
steps.cue: Stay low. Hips don't bob up and down.

steps.text: Ladder pattern: in-in-out-out, imagined ladder, 60 seconds.
steps.cue: Precision over speed. Each foot lands where it should.
Right foot crosses left, then left crosses right. Stay smooth.
Same pattern, looking over the shoulder.
Hips rotate, shoulders stay square.
The work has been done. Let it settle.

steps.text: Stand tall. Three slow nasal breaths.
steps.cue: Settle the system before you ask it to work.

steps.text: Right hand to left knee, alternating.
steps.cue: Slow enough to feel each crossing.

steps.text: Elbow to opposite knee with rotation.
steps.cue: The torso turns. Not just the limbs.

steps.text: Slow march, opposite arm and leg lifting together.
steps.cue: Find the rhythm. Don't rush it.

steps.text: Eyes closed. Notice the body in space.
steps.cue: Stillness is part of the work.

steps.text: Single-leg stance, left, eyes open, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Tripod foot. Soft knee.

steps.text: Single-leg stance, right, eyes open, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Compare the sides. Notice the difference.
Without sight, the proprioceptors take over.
Stay calm with the wobble. It's information.

steps.text: Single-leg with reach, left side, slow, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Reach across the body, then back. Move from the hip.

steps.text: Single-leg with reach, right side, slow, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Smooth, controlled, full range.

steps.text: Stand on both feet. Notice how they feel now.
steps.cue: The work changes the system. Pay attention.

secondary.name: Quadruped Control
secondary.mantra: The contralateral pattern is the foundation

steps.text: On hands and knees. Find a flat back.
steps.cue: Wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.

steps.text: Lift opposite arm and leg, hold 5 seconds. Switch.
steps.cue: Don't twist. The trunk stays quiet.

steps.text: Slow bird-dog, drawing a line forward and back.
steps.cue: The reach is long. The trunk doesn't move.

steps.text: Bear position. Hover knees one inch off the floor.
steps.cue: Tight core. Quiet hips.

steps.text: Bear walk forward, 6 steps, backward, 6 steps.
steps.cue: Knees stay low and parallel to the floor.
Let the spine release.

secondary.name: Eye-Tracking Practice
secondary.mantra: The eyes are part of the nervous system

steps.text: Sit tall. Eyes soft. Three breaths.
steps.cue: Calm body, calm gaze.

steps.text: Smooth pursuit. Track your thumb left to right, slowly.
steps.cue: Head still. Only the eyes move.
Slow. Notice if the eyes jump.

steps.text: Saccades. Look from one fixed point to another, snap.
steps.cue: Sharp transitions. Land on the target.

steps.text: Near-far focus. Thumb close, then a point across the room.
steps.cue: The lens of the eye is a muscle. It needs practice too.

steps.text: Close the eyes. Soft palming for 60 seconds.
steps.cue: Cup the eyes. Breathe. Release.

steps.text: Standing. Slow head rolls, three each direction.
steps.cue: Move slowly enough to feel each vertebra.

steps.text: Cat-cow, standing. Lead with the chest, then the tail.
steps.cue: Wave through the spine. Don't fold at one segment.

steps.text: Standing spinal waves. Roll up from a forward fold.
steps.cue: One vertebra at a time. Last to come up is the head.
Reach through the top arm. Long sides of the body.
Rotate from the chest, not the hips.

steps.text: Stand still. Feel the spine settle.
steps.cue: The movement leaves a quiet behind it.

secondary.name: Slow Mobility Flow
secondary.mantra: Range you control is range you own

steps.text: Shoulder controlled rotations, slow, both directions.
steps.cue: Move through the full circle. No shortcuts.

steps.text: Hip controlled rotations, standing, both legs.
steps.cue: Lift the knee, draw the largest circle you can.
Often-neglected joint. Give it attention.
End range matters. Push slightly past comfort.
Each vertebra moves independently. Slow.
The body feels different. Let it.

steps.text: Stand. Tap right hand to left shoulder, left hand to right shoulder.
steps.cue: Hands cross the midline. Slow at first.
Find a tempo. Stay precise.

steps.text: Opposite-side reaches. Right arm reaches left, foot taps right.
steps.cue: Coordinate hand and foot. Don't let one rush the other.

steps.text: Two-object switching. Hold something in each hand. Pass them across.
steps.cue: The brain has to think for both sides at once.

steps.text: Tracing letters in the air, both hands at once, mirror image.
steps.cue: Right hand writes forward, left writes mirror.

steps.text: Hands at sides. Soft gaze. Settle.
steps.cue: The system has been challenged. Let it integrate.

secondary.name: Posture & Alignment Reset
secondary.mantra: The body knows alignment when you ask it

steps.text: Wall stand. Heels, hips, shoulders, head against the wall.
steps.cue: Notice what doesn't touch. That's the information.

steps.text: Step away from the wall. Hold the alignment.
steps.cue: Carry the wall with you for 30 seconds.
Shoulders down and back. Pinch a small space between the blades.
Lengthen the back of the neck. Don't push the chin forward.

steps.text: Slow march in place with tall posture, 60 seconds.
steps.cue: The posture survives the movement, not just the stillness.

steps.text: Stand. Three slow breaths. Notice the height.
steps.cue: Carry this for the next hour.
Notice the contact with the ground.
Backward, deliberate, full circles.

steps.text: Cross-touch, opposite hand to opposite knee.
steps.cue: Slow rhythm. Both sides equal.
The work has happened. Let it settle.

steps.text: Stand on the left foot, 45 seconds.
steps.cue: Tripod foot. Look at one fixed point.
Compare with the left. Notice the difference.
Without sight, the system gets honest.

steps.text: Hold a finger close. Focus on it.
steps.cue: Sharp focus. Notice the strain.

steps.text: Look across the room at the farthest point. Hold.
steps.cue: The lens relaxes. Feel that.
Each shift is a small reset.

steps.text: Soft eyes, wide gaze. Take everything in.
steps.cue: Peripheral awareness.

steps.text: Close the eyes. Cup with palms, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Darkness is rest for the eyes.

micro.name: Foot Awareness
micro.mantra: The feet are how you know the ground

steps.text: Stand barefoot if possible. Spread the toes.
steps.cue: Each toe with its own space.

steps.text: Roll through the foot. Heel, outside edge, ball, big toe.
steps.cue: Slow roll. Feel each part contact the ground.

steps.text: Tripod balance. Equal weight on three points.
steps.cue: Big toe, little toe, heel. All three pressing.
Up slow, down slower.
The feet have woken up.

micro.name: Cross-Body Wake-Up
micro.mantra: Cross the midline, wake the brain

steps.text: Right hand to left knee, slow, 10 reps.
steps.cue: Reach across the body's center line.

steps.text: Left hand to right knee, slow, 10 reps.
steps.cue: Same pattern, opposite side.

steps.text: Right elbow to left knee, lifting, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Twist through the trunk.

steps.text: Left elbow to right knee, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Equal effort both sides.
Brain is awake. Move into the day.

steps.text: Cat-cow on hands and knees, 10 reps slow.
steps.cue: Lead with the tail, then the head. Wave.

steps.text: Thread the needle, left, hold 20 seconds.
steps.cue: Reach the right hand under the left. Soften.

steps.text: Thread the needle, right, hold 20 seconds.
steps.cue: Both sides need this.
Long exhales. Let the spine release.

steps.text: Stand ready. Toes light, knees soft.
steps.cue: Athletic stance. Ready to move.
Forward, back, side, diagonal. Don't repeat.
Notice how alert the system feels now.

steps.text: Reaction starts. Move sudden, then stop.
steps.cue: Sudden burst, full stop. Practice the brake.
Calm again.

micro.name: Vestibular Reset
micro.mantra: The inner ear wakes with movement

steps.text: Stand. Slow head turns, left and right, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Eyes follow the head movement.
Up and down. Full range.

steps.text: Walk in a small circle, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Look forward, not down.
The system finds neutral.
The vestibular system rests.
Often forgotten, often stiff.
Foundation joints. Give them attention.
Big circles. Full range.
Lift the knee, draw a circle in the air.

steps.text: Neck circles, very slow, half circles only.
steps.cue: Side to side. No back rolls.

steps.text: Stand tall. Three slow nasal breaths.
steps.cue: Settle the system.

steps.text: Soft gaze ahead. Notice the breathing.
steps.cue: Don't change it. Just notice.

steps.text: Close the eyes. Stay upright. Feel the body sway.
steps.cue: Tiny adjustments are happening. They are the practice.

steps.text: Open the eyes. Slow look around.
steps.cue: Take in the room with quiet attention.

primary.name: Lower Body Strength Foundation
primary.mantra: Stop one rep short of failure

steps.cue: Full depth. Find the bottom position you trust.
Brace the core. Drive through the whole foot.
Same depth as set 1. Same control.
If form drops, stop the set.
Last set. Quality, not just completion.
Hinge from the hips. Long spine. Hamstrings load.

steps.text: Reverse lunge, 3 sets × 10 reps each leg.
steps.cue: Step back, drop the back knee. Both sides equal.
Squeeze at the top. Don't arch the lower back.
Sit. Breathe. The work is done.

primary.name: Upper Body Push-Pull
primary.mantra: Pull as hard as you push

steps.text: Warm-up. Arm circles, scapular push-ups, 60 seconds total.
steps.cue: Wake up the shoulders before loading them.
Full body plank. Chest to floor.
Same depth. Same tempo.
Stop one rep short of failure.
Last set. Full quality.

steps.text: Inverted row or band pull, 4 sets × 8 reps.
steps.cue: Pull the chest to the bar or hands.
Ribs down. Don't arch the back to press.
Lower back pressed flat. Long body.

steps.text: Hang from a bar, 60 seconds total.
steps.cue: Decompress the spine. Let the body lengthen.

primary.name: Conditioning Intervals
primary.mantra: Sustainable hard, not maximum hard

steps.cue: Get the heart rate up gradually.
Choose your modality: row, run, bike, or burpees.
Same effort as round 1. Don't go out too hard.
Halfway. The hardest round mentally.
Stay with the breathing. Stay sustainable.
Last round. Match the first.

steps.text: Cool down. Slow walking or easy movement.
steps.cue: Let the heart rate come down. Nasal breathing.

primary.name: Loaded Carry Circuit
primary.mantra: Carry well and you'll move well

steps.text: Warm-up. Walking with arm swings, 2 minutes.
steps.cue: Wake up the shoulders and hips.
Tall posture. Short, controlled steps. Don't lean.

steps.text: Suitcase carry, left hand only, 20 meters.
steps.cue: Don't lean toward the load. Resist the pull.

steps.text: Suitcase carry, right hand only, 20 meters.
steps.cue: Same equal posture. Both sides need this.

steps.text: Front rack carry, both hands, 30 meters.
steps.cue: Elbows up. Brace the core throughout.
Same posture as round 1.

steps.text: Round 2: suitcase carry, 20 meters each side.
steps.cue: Stay tall under uneven load.
Steady breathing. Strong frame.
Notice how the trunk feels worked.

primary.name: Hip and Posterior Chain
primary.mantra: The back of the body needs the most work

steps.text: Warm-up. Glute activation. Bird-dog, 10 reps each side.
steps.cue: Wake up the glutes before loading them.
Hinge, don't squat. Long spine.
Feel the hamstrings load.
Same hinge depth.
Last set. Quality.

steps.text: Single-leg glute bridge, 3 sets × 10 reps each.
steps.cue: Drive through the heel. Squeeze the glute hard.
Hinge to 90 degrees. Hold. Trunk and hamstrings work.
Slow. Control. Long reach.

steps.text: Lying hamstring stretch, both legs, 60 seconds.
steps.cue: Release the work you just did.

primary.name: Full-Body Movement Session
primary.mantra: Move the whole body in patterns

steps.cue: Open the hips, rotate the thoracic spine.

steps.text: Squat to overhead press, 3 sets × 10 reps.
steps.cue: Use a moderate load. Squat down, press up.

steps.text: Romanian deadlift to row, 3 sets × 8 reps.
steps.cue: Hinge, then pull. Two patterns linked.

steps.text: Reverse lunge with rotation, 3 sets × 8 each side.
steps.cue: Step back, drop the knee, rotate over the front leg.

steps.text: Push-up to renegade row, 3 sets × 6 reps.
steps.cue: Push-up, then row each side. Stable plank throughout.

steps.text: Bear crawl, 30 meters forward and back.
steps.cue: Knees hover. Quiet movement.
Decompress.
Heart rate down. Breathing slow.

steps.text: Deep squat hold, breathing through the nose.
steps.cue: Sit into the bottom. Let gravity do the work.
Internal and external rotation. Move slowly.
Same range, both sides.

steps.text: Thoracic rotations, on hands and knees.
steps.cue: Reach one arm under, then up to the sky.
Full circle. Slow. Deliberate.
Knees over toes. Push gently past comfort.
Wave the spine through full extension and flexion.

steps.text: Stand. Notice how the body feels now.
steps.cue: The work is done. The system has changed.

secondary.name: Unilateral Strength Block
secondary.mantra: Each side gets its own attention

steps.text: Warm-up. Single-leg glute bridge, 8 reps each side.
steps.cue: Wake up each side independently.

steps.text: Bulgarian split squat, left leg lead, 10 reps.
steps.cue: Front foot does most of the work. Long stance.

steps.text: Bulgarian split squat, right leg lead, 10 reps.
steps.cue: Match the depth and tempo of the left side.

steps.text: Single-leg Romanian deadlift, left leg, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Reach long. Standing leg slightly bent.

steps.text: Single-leg Romanian deadlift, right leg, 8 reps.
steps.cue: The weaker side reveals itself. That's information.
Resist the rotation. Brace the trunk.
Equal effort, both sides.

steps.text: Single-arm row, left and right, 8 each.
steps.cue: Pull the elbow back. Squeeze the shoulder blade.
Both sides now know what they have to do.

secondary.name: Isometric Strength Hold Series
secondary.mantra: Hold the position. Earn the strength

steps.cue: Thighs parallel to the floor. Stay there.
Long body, not a sagging body. Glutes squeezed.
Hips lifted high. Don't sag.
Same line, same lift, opposite side.
Squeeze the glutes hard for the entire time.
Lower back glued to the floor. Long limbs.

steps.text: Dead hang from a bar or doorframe, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Decompress the spine. Breathe.
Walking, slow cycling, light row. Build gradually.
You should be able to hold a conversation. Not a song.
Bring the heart rate down. Nasal breathing only.

secondary.name: Anti-Rotation & Core Stability
secondary.mantra: Stillness in the trunk is strength

steps.cue: Long lines. Quiet trunk.
Resist the rotation. Press out. Hold. Return.
Same control, opposite side.
Don't lean. Resist the pull on one side.
Stay tall through the load.

steps.text: Side plank with reach, left, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Reach under, then up to the sky. Hips don't drop.

steps.text: Side plank with reach, right, 8 reps.
steps.cue: Same control.
Lower back stays pressed to the floor.
The trunk has worked. Let it settle.

steps.text: Warm-up. Pogo hops in place, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Light feet. Quick contact with the ground.

steps.text: Squat jump, 5 reps. Reset between each.
steps.cue: Land soft. Absorb through the hips.

steps.text: Broad jump, 3 reps. Walk back between each.
steps.cue: Project forward. Stick the landing.

steps.text: Lateral hop, left and right, 5 each side.
steps.cue: Stick each landing. No bouncing.
Same height, same control.

steps.text: Single-leg pogo, left and right, 8 each.
steps.cue: Soft contact. Springy ankle.
The nervous system has been working. Let it cool.

steps.text: Warm-up. Slow walking with arm swings, 2 minutes.
steps.cue: Wake up the whole body.
Quiet feet. Knees hover.
Hips up. Chest leads.
Side to side. Cross-body coordination.
Plant the hands, swing the feet through.
Easy breathing.
Look between the hands.
Same form as round 1.

steps.text: Round 2: lateral crawl, 15 meters each side.
steps.cue: Smooth rhythm now.
Notice how the body feels.
Free movement before tempo.

steps.text: Tempo squat, 4 sets × 6 reps. Three seconds down, one up.
steps.cue: Count three on the way down. Pause briefly. Stand.
Same tempo. Don't rush as it gets hard.
Discipline the descent.
Last set. Don't break form.

steps.text: Tempo push-up, 3 sets × 6 reps. Three seconds down.
steps.cue: Same principle, upper body.

steps.text: Tempo row, 3 sets × 6 reps. Three seconds down.
steps.cue: Pull fast, return slow.
Tempo work is hard. Recover well.
Each toe with its own space.
Pull the ball of the foot toward the heel without curling toes.
Up slow, down slower. Full range.
Big toe, little toe, heel. Equal pressure.
Compare with the left side.
Sit. Breathe. Let the hips open.
Internal and external rotation work together.
Both sides need this.
Shift weight side to side. Stay low.
Long hamstrings. Soft knees.
Wave through every vertebra.
Right hand under left, breathe into the stretch.
Equal range both sides.
Wave between extension and flexion.

steps.text: Spinal twist on the floor, 30 seconds each side.
steps.cue: Both shoulders press toward the floor.
Heels, hips, shoulders, head against the wall.
Shoulders down and back. Pinch a small space between blades.
Lengthen the back of the neck.

steps.text: Step away from the wall. Three slow breaths.
steps.cue: Carry the alignment with you.
Long body. Glutes squeezed. Breathe.
Hips lifted. Don't sag.
Both sides need this.
Same form as the first.
Lower back pressed flat.

steps.text: Hang from a bar or doorframe, 30 seconds.
steps.cue: Let the body lengthen.
Reset the grip.
Notice the spine releasing further.
Shake out the hands.
Last one. Full decompression.

primary.name: Deep Work Block
primary.mantra: One task only

steps.text: Choose one task. Write it on paper.
steps.cue: If you can't name it in one sentence, it's not specific enough.
Out of sight is not enough. Out of room is the rule.
If the mind wanders, return without judgment. Return is the practice.
No screens during the break. Movement and far gaze only.
Pick up where you left off. Don't rewrite what you have.
Specific. Concrete. What's done?

primary.name: Strategic Thinking Block
primary.mantra: Think about it before you do anything about it

steps.text: Choose one decision or problem to think through. Paper only.
steps.cue: Write it as a question, not a statement.

steps.text: List everything you know about the situation. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Don't filter. Just dump.

steps.text: List what you don't know. 3 minutes.
steps.cue: Unknowns shape decisions more than knowns.
Even bad ones. Especially bad ones.

steps.text: Score each option: best case, worst case, most likely case. 8 minutes.
steps.cue: Three columns. Be honest about the worst case.

steps.text: Choose. Or decide what you need to know to choose. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Indecision is also a decision.

steps.text: Write the next concrete action. One sentence.
steps.cue: What is the next physical thing you do?

primary.name: Learning Acquisition Block
primary.mantra: Read less, mean more of it

steps.text: Choose one source: book, article, paper. Paper notebook ready.
steps.cue: Pick one. Not three. One.
Headings, sections, summaries. Map the territory.
Pen in hand. Note questions, not summaries.

steps.text: Stop. Close the source. Write what you remember. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Recall is where learning happens. Not while reading.

steps.text: Compare with the source. Find what you missed. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Gaps are where the next session begins.

steps.text: Write three sentences: what you learned, what surprised you, what to do with it. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Make the learning yours by stating it your own words.

steps.text: Close the notebook. The session is complete.
steps.cue: Don't review. Trust the work.

primary.name: Creative Output Block
primary.mantra: Make something. Then judge it

steps.text: Choose one creative task: write, draw, build, design. Tools ready.
steps.cue: The medium matters less than the commitment to make.
Creativity needs space without interruption.
If you stop to evaluate, you've stopped the work. Make first.

steps.text: Stop. Stand. Look at what you made.
steps.cue: Step back, literally. New perspective comes from new position.

steps.text: Note one thing you'll keep, one thing you'll change.
steps.cue: Two notes. Not a critique. A direction.

primary.name: Planning & Reflection Block
primary.mantra: Plan deliberately or be planned for

steps.text: Open a paper notebook. Date the page.
steps.cue: Paper, not screen. The hand processes differently.

steps.text: Reflect on the past week. What worked? 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Specific. Not 'productive day' — what specifically worked.
Be honest with yourself. No one else is reading this.

steps.text: Identify the three priorities for the week ahead. 8 minutes.
steps.cue: Three. Not seven. Three.

steps.text: For each priority, write the next concrete action. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Not 'work on X.' What is the actual first move?

steps.text: Schedule the actions. Put them in a calendar. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Unscheduled intentions don't survive contact with reality.
The plan is set. Now you can trust it and move on.

steps.text: Choose one text. Open it. Pen in hand.
steps.cue: Physical book and physical pen if possible.
If you find yourself skimming, slow down. Re-read the line.

steps.text: Write three sentences about what you read.
steps.cue: Your words, not the text's words.
The session ends here. Don't carry it into your phone.

steps.text: Choose something to remember: a list, a passage, a set of facts.
steps.cue: Pick something concrete. 8-12 items.
Don't just look. Build associations.

steps.text: Cover it. Write everything you remember from memory. 5 minutes.
steps.cue: Don't peek. The struggle is where learning happens.
Notice what didn't stick.
Second pass should be cleaner. The brain learns through retrieval.

secondary.name: Problem Solving Practice
secondary.mantra: The shape of the problem matters more than the answer

steps.text: Choose one problem: a puzzle, a math problem, a logic challenge.
steps.cue: Hard enough that the answer isn't obvious.

steps.text: Read it carefully. Understand what's being asked.
steps.cue: Most problem-solving failures are reading failures.

steps.text: Think about the structure. What kind of problem is this?
steps.cue: Pattern matching beats brute force.
Show the work. Don't try to do it in your head.

steps.text: Reflect. What was hard? What pattern emerged?
steps.cue: The reflection is where the skill develops.

steps.text: Open a dual n-back app or use a manual variant.
steps.cue: Brain.fm, Dual N-Back Pro, or similar.

steps.text: Set to your current level. Don't go easier than yesterday.
steps.cue: Train at the edge of capability.
If your accuracy drops below 80%, the level is right.
Track over weeks, not days.

secondary.name: Slow Writing Practice
secondary.mantra: Write to think, not to publish

steps.text: Open a notebook or document. Pick one question.
steps.cue: Examples: What do I really think about X? What am I avoiding?
Don't edit. Don't delete. Keep the hand moving.
Notice what surprised you.

steps.text: Underline one sentence that matters. Close it.
steps.cue: One sentence. Just one.

secondary.name: Note Synthesis
secondary.mantra: Notes are useful only if you use them

steps.text: Open recent notes from any source: meetings, books, research.
steps.cue: Pick a small batch, not your whole archive.
Don't summarize yet. Just read.
What links these? What's a thread that runs through?

steps.text: Write three sentences synthesizing what you found.
steps.cue: Synthesis is creation, not summary.
If you can't choose, the problem isn't tabs.
No tab switching. No checking anything.
Both are valid. Just decide intentionally.

micro.name: Memory Snack
micro.mantra: Recall before you reach for the answer

steps.text: Pick something you learned today. Don't look it up.
steps.cue: A name, a fact, a method, a quote.
Effort to recall is what strengthens it.
Notice the gaps without judging.
Tomorrow, try again.
Brief, focused, complete.
Random. Don't pick one you've used before.

steps.text: Subtract 7 repeatedly. Out loud or written.
steps.cue: Don't rush. Accuracy first.

steps.text: Multiply two double-digit numbers in your head.
steps.cue: Break it into parts. 23 × 14 = (23 × 10) + (23 × 4).

steps.text: Estimate something — a price, a count, a distance.
steps.cue: Estimate first, then check. Build the muscle.
The brain is warmer now.

steps.text: Identify one small decision you've been delaying.
steps.cue: Not a major life choice. A small one.
Even 'do nothing' is an option to write down.
Decision fatigue is real. Decide and conserve energy for what matters.
If there is no next action, the decision wasn't really made.
Done. Move on.

steps.text: Open a paper notebook or notes app.
steps.cue: One place where ideas live. Always the same place.

steps.text: Brain dump for 3 minutes. Anything on your mind.
steps.cue: No structure. No editing. Capture only.

steps.text: Circle the one idea worth returning to.
steps.cue: Trust your instinct on which one it is.
You've cleared the head. Now move on.

micro.name: Visual Focus Practice
micro.mantra: Train the gaze, train the mind

steps.text: Sit. Pick one small object across the room.
steps.cue: Something with detail. A leaf, a corner, a texture.

steps.text: Look at it. Don't think about it. 90 seconds.
steps.cue: When the mind wanders, return to the object.

steps.text: Close eyes. Picture the object in detail.
steps.cue: Reconstruct it. The texture, the color, the shape.
Notice what your memory missed.

steps.text: Close eyes one more time. Soft breath. Done.
steps.cue: The mind is sharper now.

primary.name: Extended Meditation
primary.mantra: Return is the practice

steps.cue: Sit upright but not stiff. Find a posture you can hold.
Don't change the breath. Just notice it.

steps.text: Attention to the breath at the nose.
steps.cue: When the mind wanders, return without judgment. Wandering is part of the practice.

steps.text: Mind wanders, return to the breath.
steps.cue: Each return is a rep. The practice is the return.
Take in the room with quiet attention.

primary.name: Body Scan Practice
primary.mantra: The body knows what the mind doesn't

steps.text: Lie down or sit. Eyes closed.
steps.cue: Settle into the support beneath you.

steps.text: Attention to the feet. Notice without changing.
steps.cue: Temperature, weight, contact.

steps.text: Move attention up the legs, slow.
steps.cue: Calves, knees, thighs. Each section gets attention.
Often holds tension we don't notice.
Where breath and emotion live.
Each finger separately if you can.
Soften the jaw. Soften the eyes.
The body as one piece.

steps.text: Open the eyes. Stay still a moment.
steps.cue: Carry the awareness with you.

primary.name: Morning Intention Practice
primary.mantra: Set the day before it sets you

steps.text: Sit with a notebook. Eyes can be open or closed.
steps.cue: Settle before you write.
Arrival before action.

steps.text: Write: how do you want to feel today? Three words.
steps.cue: Not what you want to do. How you want to feel.

steps.text: Write: what is today's first priority? One sentence.
steps.cue: If you do only one thing, what is it?

steps.text: Write: who could you support today? One person.
steps.cue: Brief. A text, a call, a thought.

steps.text: Close the notebook. Three slow breaths.
steps.cue: The day is named. Begin.

primary.name: Loving-Kindness Practice
primary.mantra: Goodwill is a practice, not a feeling

steps.cue: Settle.

steps.text: Bring yourself to mind. Wish: may I be well, may I be at peace.
steps.cue: Start with yourself. The well doesn't fill what isn't there.

steps.text: Bring someone you love to mind. Same wish.
steps.cue: Picture them clearly. Mean the wish.

steps.text: Bring a neutral person to mind. Same wish.
steps.cue: Someone you barely know. The clerk, a neighbor.

steps.text: Bring someone difficult to mind. Same wish.
steps.cue: This is the practice. May they be well.

steps.text: Extend the wish to all beings.
steps.cue: Beyond people you can name.
Carry the goodwill into the day.

primary.name: Coherent Breathing Block
primary.mantra: Breath is the lever

steps.cue: Settle into the seat.

steps.text: Inhale 5 seconds, exhale 5 seconds. Four cycles.
steps.cue: Find the rhythm. Equal in, equal out.
When the rhythm wavers, return. The rhythm is the practice.

steps.text: Slow it down. Inhale 6, exhale 6. 4 minutes.
steps.cue: Slower breathing, slower nervous system.

steps.text: Sit in stillness. Three natural breaths.
steps.cue: Notice the calm.

steps.text: Paper and pen. Not a screen.
steps.cue: Hand-writing engages different processing than typing.
Specific. Not 'good day' — what specifically went well.
Honest. No performance.

steps.text: Write: what you want for tomorrow.
steps.cue: Brief. Concrete. Three things at most.

steps.text: Write: one thing you're grateful for.
steps.cue: Specific gratitude. Name it.
The day is processed. Let it go.

steps.text: Sit comfortably. Eyes closed or soft gaze.
steps.cue: Settle.

steps.text: Inhale 4. Hold 4. Exhale 4. Hold 4. Three rounds.
steps.cue: Find the rhythm.
If the rhythm slips, restart. The breathing trains the system.
Return to spontaneous breathing. Notice the calm.

secondary.name: Gratitude Practice
secondary.mantra: Gratitude is specific or it's nothing

steps.text: Sit. Notebook ready or just close the eyes.
steps.cue: Either method works.

steps.text: Bring to mind three things from today.
steps.cue: Specific. Not 'family.' One specific moment with one person.

steps.text: For each: what made it good?
steps.cue: The reason matters. Don't just name. Examine.

steps.text: Notice one thing you usually take for granted.
steps.cue: The cup of coffee. The hot shower. The body that worked today.
Carry it.

secondary.name: Connection Practice
secondary.mantra: Reach out before the impulse fades

steps.text: Bring someone to mind you've been meaning to reach out to.
steps.cue: Trust the first name that came up.
No judgment. Just notice.
Not a manifesto. A simple acknowledgment.

steps.text: Notice how it feels to have done it.
steps.cue: Most resistance is anticipation.

steps.text: Bring one more person to mind. Same.
steps.cue: While you're warm, do another.
Connection is built in small actions.

secondary.name: Difficult Emotion Practice
secondary.mantra: Feel it, then it can move

steps.text: Sit. Close the eyes. Three breaths.
steps.cue: Settle the body before approaching the mind.

steps.text: Bring to mind a recent difficult feeling.
steps.cue: Not the worst. Something present and uncomfortable.

steps.text: Where does it sit in the body?
steps.cue: Tightness in the chest. Heaviness in the gut. Heat in the face.
Don't try to dissolve it. Make space around it.

steps.text: Notice if it shifts. If it doesn't, that's also fine.
steps.cue: The acknowledgment is the work, not the dissolution.

steps.text: Soft eyes. Slow breaths. Open the eyes.
steps.cue: Difficult feelings deserve attention, not avoidance.

steps.text: Find a quiet space, indoor or outdoor. Stand.
steps.cue: Settle into the body before moving.

steps.text: Walk slowly. Attention on the feet.
steps.cue: Lifting, moving, placing. Each phase deliberate.

steps.text: Notice the breath. Don't change it.
steps.cue: Walking and breathing in conversation.
Take it in without grasping.

steps.text: Return to the feet. Walk slowly until done.
steps.cue: The walk has a beginning, middle, end. Each part different.
Sit or stand. Soften the shoulders.
The longer exhale signals safety to the nervous system.
Return, then rest.

steps.text: Stop whatever you're doing. Stand or sit.
steps.cue: Pause is a practice.
Fill the lungs. Don't rush.

steps.text: Second breath: longer exhale than inhale.
steps.cue: Breathe out twice as long as you breathe in.
The system has been signaled. Return to the day.
Arrival before reflection.

steps.text: One thing from today: what worked?
steps.cue: Specific. One moment, not a category.

steps.text: One person from today: who helped?
steps.cue: Even small help. Even unspoken.

steps.text: One thing you're carrying: be glad for it.
steps.cue: Even the difficult things are evidence of being alive.
Drop into the body.

steps.text: Notice the feet. Where they touch.
steps.cue: Bottom up. Foundation first.

steps.text: Notice the seat or the legs holding weight.
steps.cue: How is gravity meeting you?

steps.text: Notice the chest rising and falling.
steps.cue: Breath without changing it.

steps.text: Notice the head. The face. The jaw.
steps.cue: Soften any tension found.

steps.text: Open the eyes. Carry the awareness.
steps.cue: The day continues. So does the body.
Trust the first person who came up.
Just thinking of you. Just hi. Just thanks.
Notice how it feels.
Connection happens in moments like this.
Pause the activity.
Equal sides. Find the rhythm.
Don't rush. The pace is the medicine.
Notice the calm.
Arrival.

steps.text: What am I feeling right now? Find one word.
steps.cue: Anxious. Tired. Hopeful. Neutral. Whatever it is.

steps.text: Where does the feeling sit in the body?
steps.cue: Locate it. Specific.

steps.text: One slow breath into that place. Done.
steps.cue: Acknowledgment is enough.
Break the focused gaze.

steps.text: Soft, wide gaze. Look without focusing.
steps.cue: Take in the whole field of vision.
Distance relaxes the eye muscles.

steps.text: Three slow breaths. Continue with what you were doing.
steps.cue: Reset complete.
